newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finland's Nokia plans solar handset.
newsitem.headline: Finland's Nokia plans solar handset.

text.p: Nokia Oy, Europe's largest mobile phone maker, said Wednesday it will soon launch a handset with a unique solar-powered battery which it says will be "the most mobile phone under the sun."

Claiming "another first" in the mobile industry, Nokia said its new 1611 model, an upgrade of the 1610 handset which is currently targeted at broad consumer markets, could be charged simply by leaving it in a sunny place.
"You don't need plugs or anything like that," said spokeswoman Liisa Nyyssonen.
Nokia said it plans to start distributing the new phone in European markets at the end of January.
However, the solar batteries will not become available in large volumes until April -- which is about when solar charging would become a viable option, at least in Finland.

With Helsinki under a thick blanket of cloud Wednesday afternoon, Nyyssonen said solar charging would be unlikely to work. The actual amount of light needed by the new phone would vary but it would work on a partly cloudy day, she said.
